proposal_assessment: Classification. N1 is technical legibility: a framing crop makes the claim-bound figure 98.82% (c4) display as 8.82% and then '2%' beside 'accuracy', while the narration states the limit. That is the same category as classified M1, and it is not motion, pacing, story or style. BOUNDED_CREATIVE_RELEASE lists readability, comprehension and misleading implications as non-deferrable. The sweep adds no further mandatory finding. Its other confirmed crossings fall into three groups. Blank paper or a pushpin under the chip or past an edge carries no text. 'Field result' crosses an edge only during the designed slide-in entries. B's result card passes over the figure for about 5 frames as a moving transient with no misreadable number. All are reported for the phone review. So N1 alone is correct and covered exactly once. Minimality. The director's correction is renderer-only, confined to the no-field-card branch and detail framing (A's s8-shot-1 only; B's close framing has push 0 already), and changes no board, script, claims, caption, mix or timing. That is the minimal fix. One problem: the brief requires the push to stay a visible push, and by my arithmetic that is close to infeasible together with its own margins (see code_assessment). Read literally, it could push the builder into thinner margins or a failed search. Before begin-repair, amend the expected result to allow a held or near-held framing (total extra scale about 1.03 or less, focus recentred), since the stamp coming down from 50.18 to 50.93 s carries the shot's action. Template bookkeeping: failure_evidence and its sha256 are still FILLED_AFTER_CLASSIFICATION. StreetHubSupport is declared as a changed input under an r15f/baseline path. If it stays byte-identical (after equals before 444be8ad), that is harmless but not needed. Remove it if the controller allows, to keep the batch minimal.

recurrence: Stable family document-handling, second correction in it. The first was R15e (s7-detail-safe-area-framing), which classified M1 and M2 on film c0aee5b3 and resolved them in code for s7-shot-2 in both treatments. R15f's s8-detail-safe-area-framing is not a relabel to evade recurrence: it keeps the same family, targets a different branch and shot (no-field-card, s8-shot-1, A only) with its own geometry, and the failed R15e mechanism did not fail on its own target. Plainly, though, it is the same method applied to the same defect class. The s8 crop already existed in the rejected film c0aee5b3 and should have been in R15e's one consolidated correction. My critic-34 classification chose to defer it as report-only, and I record that as my error. In my judgment this is a completion of the first consolidated correction, not a second rejection of a corrected mechanism. If the controller counts family recurrences, this is the second in document-handling, and any third same-family crop must go to the independent pivot rule. repair.md says camera offsets and easing changes are not a pivot, so R15f must not be described as one. It differs from earlier mechanisms (announcement-scoped-absence-claim, the physical-water-sensor-range-map pictures pivot, measured-runtime and opening-binding repairs), which concerned other defect kinds. The sweep found no other same-class crop of printed text, so a single R15f batch should close the family.
